battle.name: 敬盤陀
battle.brief: 大業十一年（615）十二月，詔民部尚書樊子蓋發關中兵數萬擊絳賊敬盤陀等。樊子蓋不分臮否、自汾水以北焚盡村塢、坑殺降者，叛眾反而愈聚愈多；朝廷改命李淵，淵以招撫為先，賊眾前後數萬人降，餘黨散入它郡。卡面羅馬標槍屬前二世紀羅馬軍團，與此役相隔七百餘年，並非當場所用。

kit.name: 羅馬標槍
kit.history: 半米長的投槍，槍幹中空。捅穿盾之後就折斷，敵人只能帶著半截槍退回掩體。

countries: 這場衝突發生在大業十一年（615）末的晉南絳郡，是隋朝中央與一支盤踞村塢的流民武裝之間的鎮壓戰，交戰雙方在《資治通鑑》卷182與《隋書》本紀中都只佔寥寥數語。隋朝一方以中央京師的調度為骨架：民部尚書樊子蓋奉詔所發的「關中兵數萬」是主力，來自關內各郡的郡兵、縣兵、屯田戍卒與臨時募兵，隸屬京師宿衛體系與長安、周原一線的駐軍；地方上則是汾州、絳州、晉州各縣的鄉兵與守令所部的武裝，負責守城、護糧道與追捕散眾。李淵以山西河東撫慰大使的身份駐節河東，握有黶陟、選補郡縣文武官的權柄，於是他接手後能同時動用兵與吏。另一方是《通鑑》所稱的「絳賊敬盤陀等」，《隋書》本紀作「敬盤陀、柴保昌」，是一群由括戶、逃戶、逃卒與饑民組成的聚眾，無常備編制與官號，以汾水以北的村塢與山寨為據點，人數被記為數萬。此外同一年的背景還有北方的突厥——七月始畢可汗率騎數十萬逼近乘輿，雁門被圍四十餘日；東南的朱粲眾至十餘萬、自號迦樓羅王，李子通渡淮與杜伏威合勢；山東的魏騏驎於十月聚眾萬餘寇魯郡。隋朝的兵力被四處抽走，這是絳郡一線久不能平的直接原因。
countriesEn: This clash took place in the Jiang commandery of southern Shanxi in the closing months of the Daye eleventh year (615). It was a suppression war fought between the Sui court and a body of refugees entrenched in fortified villages, and in the Zizhi Tongjian, volume 182, as well as in the annals of the Sui shu, each side occupies only a few lines. The Sui side was built on the dispatch of the capital: the main force was the "tens of thousands of Guanzhong troops" which the Minister of Revenue Fan Zigae was ordered to raise, drawn from the levies of the prefectures and counties inside Guanzhong, from garrison and farm troops, and from men hastily recruited, all belonging to the capital garrison system around Chang'an and the Zhouyuan plain; on the local level stood the village militia of the counties of Fen, Jiang and Jin zhou and the armed followers of the magistrates, responsible for holding walls, escorting grain convoys and hunting down scattered rebels. Li Yuan, then Pacification Commissioner for Shanxi and Hedong, was based on the Hedong side with the authority to assess officials and to appoint and replace the civil and military officers of prefectures and counties, so that when he took over he could use soldiers and clerks at once. The other side were the "Jiang rebels Jingpantuo and the rest" of the Tongjian, recorded in the Sui shu annals as "Jingpantuo and Chai Baochang": a gathering made up of people uprooted by the census registers, runaway households, deserters and famine victims, with no permanent establishment and no official titles, holding the fortified villages and mountain fastnesses north of the Fen river, and recorded as numbering several tens of thousands. The background of the same year runs on all sides: in the north the Turks, for in the seventh month the qaghan Qibi led tens of thousands of riders at the emperor's convoy and besieged Yanmen for more than forty days; in the southeast Zhu Can had gathered more than a hundred thousand men and styled himself king of the rakshasa, while Li Zitong crossed the Huai and joined forces with Du Fuwei; in Shandong Wei Qilin raised more than ten thousand men in the tenth month and raided Lu commandery. Sui troops were being pulled away in every direction, and that is the direct reason the Jiang front could not be settled.
people: 主戰雙方的名字都留在史書裡。官軍主將樊子蓋，時任民部尚書，《通鑑》記他「不分臮否，自汾水之北，村塢盡焚之，賊有降者皆坑之」，是一個以手段酷烈換取迅速平亂的人；史書記這場絳賊之亂久久不能剋，朝廷隨即罷他而另換將。接手者是李淵，這一年他以衛尉少卿出為山西河東撫慰大使，承製黶陟、選補郡縣文武官，《通鑑》稱他御眾寬簡、人多附之，隋煬帝卻因他相貌奇異、又有人說名應圖讖而頗忌之；他在絳賊一事上只用招撫一策便收束了兵亂。叛方首領是敬盤陀，《隋書》本紀記作「敬盤陀、柴保昌」，《通鑑》則概稱「絳賊敬盤陀等」，二人的生平都極少留下記載，連名字的寫法也只在兩種史書裡並存。同一條時間線上還排得出同年並起的人物：正月的齊郡賊帥顏宣政，十月的彭城人魏騏驎，以及樊子蓋治下各州縣的官吏。河東軍中另有李淵次子李世民，他當年十六，隸雲定興屯衛，以白晝張旌旗數十里、夜間擊鉦鼓相應的疑兵之計助雁門解圍，與絳賊之戰並無直接關係，卻在同一支河東軍伍裡長大，兩年後他會代替父親成為唐軍的主帥。
peopleEn: The names on both sides survive in the historical record. The Sui commander was Fan Zigae, then Minister of Revenue; the Tongjian records that he "made no distinction between the innocent and the guilty, burned every village north of the Fen river from the Fen upwards, and put every rebel who surrendered into a pit" — a man who meant to end the disorder quickly by the harshest means. The history records that this Jiang rebellion could not be put down for a long time, and the court soon removed him and appointed another. The man who took over was Li Yuan, who that year left the post of Commandant of the Palace Guard for the office of Pacification Commissioner for Shanxi and Hedong, with the authority to assess officials and to appoint and replace the civil and military officers of the prefectures and counties; the Tongjian says of him that he ruled his men leniently and that men flocked to him, while Emperor Yang of Sui was wary of him because of his strange physiognomy and because people said his name answered to a prophecy in the charts. In the matter of the Jiang rebels Li Yuan used nothing but a policy of amnesty and finished the war. The rebel leader was Jingpantuo, recorded in the annals of the Sui shu as "Jingpantuo and Chai Baochang" and generically in the Tongjian as "the Jiang rebels Jingpantuo and the rest"; almost nothing is known of the two men, and even the spelling of the name survives in only two sets of annals. Other figures of the same year line up on the same timeline: the bandit chief Yan Xuanzheng of Qi commandery in the first month, Wei Qilin of Pengcheng in the tenth month, and the officials of the prefectures and counties under Fan Zigae. The Hedong army also contained Li Yuan's second son Li Shimin, then sixteen years old, who served under the garrison commander Yun Dingxing and helped relieve Yanmen by a ruse: banners stretched for tens of li by day, drums and gongs beaten by night to keep the Turk camp confused. He had nothing to do with the Jiang fighting, but he grew up inside the same Hedong army, and two years later he would replace his father as commander in chief of the Tang forces.
kits: 卡面這件羅馬標槍（pilum）與本役沒有直接關係：它是前二世紀羅馬共和國末期至帝國初期軍團的標準投射兵器，半米長，槍幹中空，槍頭與柄的接合處特製成空心套管，擲出後一旦捅穿盾牌，槍幹就會在套管處折斷，敵人只能帶著半截槍退回掩體再去拔；羅馬軍隊以標槍兵與劍盾兵配成一體，標槍由軍需官按單位配發，前線的木箱裝滿標槍，打空了就必須退到後方補充。與本役真正同處戰場的投射兵器是隋軍的弓、弩與標箭：步卒用角弓與木弓，攻城與守城倚仗蹶張弩、床弩、長槊與矛，近戰用環首刀；甲胄方面，隋制分明光鎧、銅甲、札甲與皮甲，隊長以上才披全甲，州郡兵與義民多以皮甲葛布為護。叛方是流民聚眾，能用的只有粗弓梟矢、竹木矛、鋤叉改製的兵器與少量皮甲，既無成型的弩機，也無成形的防具，食糧多靠劫掠與村塢的存糧，因此最怕糧道斷絕與屯田不能恢復。中文裡「標槍」與「標箭」共用一個「標」字，是譯名的巧合：隋代的標箭是帶羽的長桿箭，羅馬標槍則是短投矛，形制與用法都不同。
kitsEn: The Roman pilum on the card has no direct bearing on this campaign. It was the standard missile of the Roman army from the late Republic into the early Empire, about half a metre long with a hollow shaft, and the joint between the head and the shaft was made as a hollow socket, so that once the weapon had been thrown and had punched through a shield the shaft would break at that socket, and the enemy could only drag himself back behind cover with half a pilum still sticking in the shield. The Romans paired pilum troops with sword-and-shield infantry; the javelins were issued by the quartermaster by unit, crates of them stood at the front, and once they were spent the front line had to fall back to be resupplied. The missiles that actually fought on this battlefield were the Sui bows, crossbows and feathered arrows: foot soldiers used small horn and wooden bows, sieges and defences relied on the drawn crossbow, the heavy crossbow, the long sao and the spear, and close quarters were settled with ring-pommel sabres. On armour, the Sui code distinguished the bright reflective cuirass, bronze plate, lamellar and leather; only officers of company grade and above wore the full suit, while prefectural levies and volunteers were protected by little more than leather and coarse cloth. The rebels, being a gathering of refugees, had only coarse bows with rough arrows, bamboo and wooden spears, farming implements converted into weapons, and a little leather; they had neither formed crossbow mechanisms nor organised protection, and their food came mostly from plunder and from what the village strongholds had stored, which made them most vulnerable to a cut supply line and to any failure of the farm colonies to be restored. The fact that Chinese and Latin happen to use the same word, "biao", for the pilum and for the feathered arrow is a coincidence of translation: the Sui arrow was a long shafted shaft with fletching, whereas the pilum was a short thrusting javelin, different in form and in use.
tactics: 樊子蓋的打法是焦土加拒降：他不分別良莠，自汾水之北逐個村塢掃過去，凡村塢一律焚毀，凡降者一律坑殺，企圖以摧毀據點與斷絕生路逼出「益相聚為盜」的結果——兵源非但沒有枯竭，反而因怨恨而擴大。官軍的難處在補給：關中兵數萬自長安一線出發，糧秣須沿渭水東行，渡蒲坂與龍門再折入汾水，全程數百里，冬季行軍與車載給養都拖慢腳步；一旦深入村塢密集的汾北丘陵，前線與糧隊脫節，兵再多也難以合圍。叛方的戰術是流動式的：靠村塢與山寨作掩護，以步眾為主，馬匹極少，熟悉山道與里閭的鄉民充當嚮導，官軍重兵指向一處，別處就重新聚眾。李淵接手後把重心從剿換成撫：停止焚燒村塢，對降者一律收置左右，編入麾下，以降眾自身勸誘同類歸順；同時分兵扼住汾水各渡口與通往晉陽、關中的要道，斷其流竄；以撫慰使的黶陟選補權重新派置州縣官吏，恢復汾、晉二州的屯田與編戶，把糧源與兵源一併接回官府手中。最終「賊眾多降，前後數萬人，餘黨散入它郡」，一場原本要靠殲滅才能收束的亂事，改用一次政策性轉向收場。
tacticsEn: Fan Zigae's method was scorched earth plus refusal of quarter. He made no distinction between the innocent and the guilty, worked through the villages north of the Fen one by one, burned every fortified village without exception and put every man who surrendered into a pit, in the hope of destroying the strongholds and cutting off all way of life for the rebels so as to produce the result recorded as "the people grew more bitter and gathered as bandits in even greater numbers". The source of rebel strength not only failed to dry up, it grew because of the resentment. The real difficulty for the Sui army lay in supply: tens of thousands of men marched out from the Chang'an line, and their grain had to travel east along the Wei river, be ferried past Pucheng and Longmen and then turned up the Fen, a route of several hundred li, with winter marching and wagon-borne rations slowing everything down. Once the army pushed into the hilly country north of the Fen, thick with fortified villages, the forward echelon separated from the baggage train, and no amount of numbers allowed a proper encirclement. The rebels' method was fluid: they used the villages and the mountain fastnesses as cover, marched mostly on foot, possessed very few horses, and were guided by villagers who knew the tracks and the hamlets; whenever the Sui army concentrated heavily on one place, another place gathered fresh men. When Li Yuan took over he shifted the weight of the campaign from annihilation to amnesty. He stopped the burning of the villages, received all who surrendered and placed them on either side of himself, taking them into his own ranks so that the surrendered themselves would press their fellows to come in; at the same time he split off troops to hold the fords of the Fen and the roads leading to Jinyang and into Guanzhong, to cut off the flight of the rebels; and through the assessor's and appointor's authority of the pacification commission he redistributed the officials of the prefectures and counties and restored the farm colonies and the registered households of Fen and Jin, bringing both the food supply and the supply of soldiers back into the hands of the government. In the end, "the rebel masses came over in great numbers, several tens of thousands in all, and the remnants scattered away into the other prefectures": a disorder which had looked as though it could only be ended by annihilation was instead closed off by a single change of policy.
data: 可核對的數字不多。官軍方面，《通鑑》明言樊子蓋所發為「關中兵數萬」，而未記確數；《隋書》本紀敘這場絳賊之亂，則有「經年不能剋」之語，指的是整樁亂事久久不靖，並非單指某一次進剿。叛方，《隋書》本紀記敬盤陀、柴保昌等聚眾作亂、陷絳郡，眾數萬，具體人數不詳。收官一方的成果有明文：降者「前後數萬人」，餘黨散入它郡。同一年的時間軸可作對照：七月突厥始畢可汗率騎數十萬謀襲乘輿，雁門被圍四十餘日，城中兵民十五萬口而食僅可支二旬；十月彭城人魏騏驎聚眾萬餘寇魯郡；十二月詔發關中兵數萬，此日《資治通鑑》作庚寅、《隋書》本紀作庚辰。地理上，絳郡治絳縣，即今山西新絳，汾水自北而南流經城外，龍門渡口在縣境以南約六十公里，絳縣至晉陽約二百八十公里，至長安約二百五十至三百公里；按隋唐軍隊日行三十至五十里估算，關中兵由長安開到絳郡前線需十日至二十日。汾水全程逾七百公里，順流而下至龍門方可轉入黃河水路，這條線既是官軍的糧道，也是叛眾南逃的出口。
dataEn: Few figures can be checked. On the Sui side the Tongjian states plainly that Fan Zigae was given "tens of thousands of Guanzhong troops", and records no exact number; the annals of the Sui shu, describing this Jiang business, use the phrase that it could not be put down for a year, which refers to the whole affair dragging on, not to any single raid. For the rebels, the Sui shu annals record that Jingpantuo, Chai Baochang and the rest rose in revolt, seized the Jiang commandery and numbered several tens of thousands, with no exact count given. The results of the side that closed the business stand in clear text: those who came over were "several tens of thousands in all", and the remnants scattered into the other prefectures. The chronology of the same year provides a frame: in the seventh month the Turk qaghan Qibi led tens of thousands of riders against the emperor's convoy and Yanmen was besieged for more than forty days, with 150,000 soldiers and civilians in the city and grain for only twenty days; in the tenth month Wei Qilin of Pengcheng raised more than ten thousand men and raided Lu commandery; on the gengyin day of the twelfth month the order went out to raise the Guanzhong troops. Geographically, the Jiang commandery had its seat at Jiang county, in what is now Xinjiang county in Shanxi, with the Fen river running south past the walls; the Longmen crossing lay about sixty kilometres south of the county, Jiang county was roughly 280 kilometres from Jinyang and some 250 to 300 kilometres from Chang'an, and on an estimate of thirty to fifty li of marching a day the Guanzhong troops needed ten to twenty days to reach the forward position at Jiang. The Fen runs for more than 700 kilometres in all, and only below Longmen does it join the Yellow River, so that the line of the river was at once the Sui army's grain road and the rebels' way out to the south.
cause: 大業年間三征高句麗，括戶、徵兵、興工、修運河，州縣丁壯被一遍遍抽走，關中與河東一帶又連年饑荒，逃戶與逃卒成了流民的主要來源；絳郡一帶的村塢聚居，本來就是流民賴以棲身的地方，一旦官府用兵，聚集起義只要有人點頭便可成形。直接引爆的還有樊子蓋的辦法：他奉詔討賊之後，政策不是勸降而是清剿，村塢盡焚、降者盡坑，結果正如《通鑑》所記「百姓怨憤，益相聚為盜」，把原本可以爭取的邊緣鄉里推向叛方，叛眾由數萬而膨脹，隋朝在絳郡一線的兵力卻被北方的雁門之圍、江南的朱粲與李子通、山東的魏騏驎同時牽制。朝廷的處置也說明制度的僵化：同一件事，關中兵出動一次要靠下一道詔書才換人，主將的方針出了錯，改正的代價是兵員與糧秣的重新調配；一年之後山西仍是眾起之地，說明招撫只解決了當面的兵，而沒有解決流民的生計。
causeEn: In the Daye years the Sui court campaigned against Goguryeo three times, and in between it made the census registrations harsher, pressed men into the armies, built works and cut the Grand Canal, so that the adult males of every prefecture and county were drawn off again and again; in Guanzhong and Hedong famine followed famine, and the runaways and deserters of the countryside became the main source of the displaced. The clustered villages of the Jiang area were precisely the sort of place where such people sheltered, and once troops were in the field a rising needed nothing more than one man to say yes. What actually set the powder alight was Fan Zigae's method. His policy after receiving the order was not amnesty but clearance: villages burned, surrenderers put in pits, and the result was exactly what the Tongjian records — "the people grew bitter and angry and gathered together as bandits in even greater numbers". The doubtful fringe, who might have been won over, was driven into the rebel side, and the rebel numbers grew from several tens of thousands to something larger, while the Sui force available on the Jiang line was tied down at the same time by the siege of Yanmen in the north, by Zhu Can and Li Zitong in the south-east and by Wei Qilin in Shandong. The conduct of the court also shows how rigid the system had become: a single affair needed a fresh decree to move the Guanzhong troops, and once a commander's policy went wrong the cost of correcting it was the re-allocation of men and grain; a year later Shanxi was still in arms from end to end, which shows that amnesty solved the soldiers in front of the court but not the livelihood of the displaced.
impact: 這場戰爭的結果決定了山西接下來兩年的走向。招撫成功之後，樊子蓋的焚殺之政被罷，汾、晉二州的刺史與縣吏重新派置，屯田與編戶復舊；降者前後數萬人被收編或解散，織在晉南的流民武裝暫時瓦解，絳郡一線的戰事收束。但根本的病竈並未因此除去：大業十二年（616）正月雁門人翟松柏起兵於靈丘、眾至數萬，四月甄翟兒自歷山飛起眾十萬轉寇太原，隋將潘長文出戰而戰死；東海賊盧公暹保於蒼山，朱粲又僭稱楚帝、眾至十餘萬（《通鑑》記其先自稱迦樓羅王）。同一時間，關中的薛舉也據隴西起兵，與太原的唐國公李淵隔河相望。李淵在此役中嘗到的甜頭——招撫可收兵、撫慰使可調吏、太原可徵兵——在兩年後被放大成他起兵的資本：617年他終於以太原留守的身份舉兵，618年入長安建唐。所以從長時段看，敬盤陀之亂既是一次平叛的成功，也是一次示範：它證明了在隋末，兵亂要靠改變政策而非增加殺戮才能收場，同時也把山西的兵源、馬匹與糧秣推到了下一位主角手裡。
impactEn: The outcome of this war shaped the next two years in Shanxi. After the amnesty succeeded, Fan Zigae's policy of burning was abolished, the governors and county magistrates of Fen and Jin were replaced, and the farm colonies and the registered households were put back on their feet. Tens of thousands of men who came over were taken into service or dispersed, the armed bands of the displaced in southern Shanxi broke up for the time being, and the fighting on the Jiang line was settled. But the underlying sickness was not removed. In the first month of Daye 12 (616) Zhai Songbai of Yanmen rose at Lingqiu with tens of thousands of men; in the fourth month Zhen Die'er took ten thousand followers as the Flying General of Mount Li and turned on Taiyuan, where the Sui commander Pan Changwen was killed in action; the pirate Lu Gongxian held out at Mount Cang, and Zhu Can once more proclaimed himself king of Chu with more than a hundred thousand men. At the same time Xue Ju rose in Longxi in Guanzhong, across the river from Tang gong Li Yuan at Taiyuan. What Li Yuan learned here — that amnesty can bring in soldiers, that a pacification commissioner can move officials, that Taiyuan can raise troops — was enlarged two years later into the capital of his rising: in 617 he finally took up arms as the garrison commander of Taiyuan, and in 618 he entered Chang'an and founded the Tang. Seen over the long run, the Jingpantuo rising was both a successful suppression and a demonstration: it showed that in the late Sui a rebellion had to be ended by changing policy rather than by adding to the killing, and at the same time it handed the soldiers, horses and grain of Shanxi to the next protagonist.
result: 結果有明文可稽：大業十一年十二月詔發關中兵數萬討絳賊敬盤陀等（《資治通鑑》作庚寅，《隋書》本紀作庚辰），樊子蓋不分臮否、自汾水之北焚盡村塢、坑殺降者，叛眾反而益聚；朝廷改詔以李淵代之，淵罷焚殺、改行招撫，有降者引置左右，於是「賊眾多降，前後數萬人，餘黨散入它郡」，汾、晉之間的這一支亂事就此收束，州縣的刺史與縣吏隨之重配，屯田復舊。需要說明的是，這是一場以政策轉向換來的收束，而非以會戰取勝：史書沒有記載兩軍在野外做過一次決定性的交鋏，敬盤陀本人的下場也沒有留下記載，《隋書》本紀與《通鑑》都只給出「陷絳郡、眾數萬」與「多降數萬人、餘黨散入它郡」兩組數字。餘黨散入它郡意味著武裝並未消滅，只是失去據點與首領，轉入更小的、更難追索的分散形態；三年後唐軍平定山東、河東時遇到的地方反抗，多半就是這類餘脈。
resultEn: The result stands in clear text. On the gengyin day of the twelfth month of Daye 11 the order went out to raise tens of thousands of Guanzhong troops against the Jiang rebels Jingpantuo and the rest; Fan Zigae made no distinction between the innocent and the guilty, burned the villages north of the Fen and put the surrenderers into pits, and the rebel masses grew instead; the court then changed the decree and put Li Yuan in charge, and Li Yuan stopped the burning and took up amnesty, receiving those who surrendered and keeping them on either side of himself, so that "the rebel masses came over in great numbers, several tens of thousands in all, and the remnants scattered away into the other prefectures". The disturbance on the Fen and Jin was closed off at that point, the governors and county magistrates of the prefectures and counties were redistributed, and the farm colonies were put back on their feet. It should be said that this was a settlement bought by a change of policy, not by a battle won in the field: the histories record no decisive engagement between the two armies in the open, and nothing is recorded of Jingpantuo's own fate; the Sui shu annals and the Tongjian give only two sets of figures, that the rebels seized the Jiang commandery with several tens of thousands of men, and that tens of thousands came over while the remnants scattered into the other prefectures. The scattering of the remnants means the armed force was not destroyed but deprived of its strongholds and its leaders and broken into smaller, harder-to-trace groups; when the Tang armies brought order to Shandong and Hedong three years later, much of the local resistance they met was of this kind.
